flashcards.back: Material nature is the womb of creation; God places in it the seed of consciousness, and all beings are born.
Sattva (goodness), Rajas (passion, activity), Tamas (ignorance, inertia): they bind the eternal soul to the body.
Goodness by attachment to knowledge and happiness; passion by craving for fruits; ignorance by delusion, laziness and sleep.
Clarity, knowledge and lightness shine through the senses.
Greed, restlessness, craving and endless activity.
The mode that dominates at death shapes the next birth.
One who rises above the three modes attains immortality, free from the pains of birth, old age and death.

flashcards.front: Who has gone beyond the modes?
flashcards.back: One who neither hates them when present nor longs for them when gone, and watches them unmoved.

flashcards.front: How to rise above the modes (14.26)
flashcards.back: By serving God with love and unswerving devotion: one becomes fit for Nirvana.

quiz.why: God places the seed of consciousness in it.

quiz.text: Greed and restlessness are signs of:

quiz.text: What happens to one who rises above the three modes (14.20)?

quiz.text: What cuts the bonds of the modes (14.26)?
quiz.why: Devotional love lifts one above them.
